knowledge:
- key_parameters: genomeAnnotation=A data frame containing genomic annotations with exactly 6 columns (chr, tag, start, end, strand, ID) used to annotate SVs ;; genome=A data frame containing chromosome lengths (chromosome, length) used to plot whole-genome SV distribution ;; binSize=The window size in base pairs (e.g., 1000000) used to bin SVs for whole-genome visualization
- alternatives: The package integrates predictions from BreakDancer, CNVnator, SVseq2, DELLY, Pindel, Lumpy, and softSearch, noting that combining multiple callers is superior to relying on any single method.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have structural variation predictions from one or more supported callers and want to merge them into a consensus set, annotate their impact on genes, and visualize their genomic distribution.
- pitfalls: The directory provided to readCnvnator must only contain the final output files of CNVnator. ;; The files containing predicted deletions for readSvseq must have the suffix .del. ;; The files containing predicted deletions, inversions, and duplications for readPindel must have the suffixes _D, _INV, and _TD respectively. ;; svAnnotation only accepts a data frame, so you must apply it to each component of the merged list (e.g., using llply or lapply). ;; Custom predictions from unsupported programs must be manually formatted into a data frame with exactly six columns: chromosome, pos1, pos2, size, type, and methods.

workflows.name: sv_integration_annotation_visualization
workflows.intent: Read structural variation predictions from multiple callers, merge them into a consensus set, annotate their genomic effects, and visualize their distribution.
input: svseq2 (Directory containing SVseq2 output files with .del suffix)
pindel (Directory containing Pindel output files with _D, _INV, _TD suffixes)
chr05_chr10.anno.txt (Plain text genomic annotation file with 6 columns)
chr05_chr10.genome.txt (Plain text genome chromosome length file)
workflows.stages: 1. Read predictions from individual SV callers using readBreakDancer, readCnvnator, readSvseq, readDelly, readPindel, readLumpy, and readSoftSearch. ;; 2. Integrate predictions from multiple programs using methodsMerge. ;; 3. Load genomic annotation and annotate SV effects using svAnnotation. ;; 4. Load genome chromosome lengths and plot whole-genome SV distribution using plotChromosome. ;; 5. Visualize SVs in a specific genomic region using plotRegion.
workflows.code:
breakdancer.file.path <- system.file("extdata/ZS97.breakdancer.sv",
                               package="intansv")
breakdancer <- readBreakDancer(breakdancer.file.path)
cnvnator.dir.path <- system.file("extdata/cnvnator", package="intansv")
cnvnator <- readCnvnator(cnvnator.dir.path)
svseq.dir.path <- system.file("extdata/svseq2", package="intansv")
svseq <- readSvseq(svseq.dir.path)
delly.file.path <- system.file("extdata/ZS97.DELLY.vcf", package="intansv")
delly <- readDelly(delly.file.path)
pindel.dir.path <- system.file("extdata/pindel", package="intansv")
pindel <- readPindel(pindel.dir.path)
lumpy.file.path <- system.file("extdata/ZS97.LUMPY.vcf",
                   package="intansv")
lumpy <- readLumpy(lumpy.file.path)
softSearch.file.path <- system.file("extdata/ZS97.softsearch", package="intansv")
softSearch <- readSoftSearch(softSearch.file.path)
sv_all_methods <- methodsMerge(breakdancer, pindel, cnvnator, delly, svseq)
anno.file.path <- system.file("extdata/chr05_chr10.anno.txt", package="intansv")
msu_gff_v7 <- read.table(anno.file.path, head=TRUE, as.is=TRUE)
sv_all_methods.anno <- llply(sv_all_methods,svAnnotation,
                             genomeAnnotation=msu_gff_v7)
genome.file.path <- system.file("extdata/chr05_chr10.genome.txt", package="intansv")
genome <- read.table(genome.file.path, head=TRUE, as.is=TRUE)
plotChromosome(genome, sv_all_methods,1000000)
plotRegion(sv_all_methods,msu_gff_v7, "chr05", 1, 200000)
